statements.t: "I am very pleased with our third quarter results that clearly demonstrate that investments made to build greater scale and capacity during the first half of the year, including our workforce additions, delivered the benefits we expected as productivity and efficiency improved across our operations," said Centuri President & CEO Christian Brown.

With nearly $4.8 billion of outstanding bids, including $2 billion of MSA renewals expected by year-end, we anticipate a full-year book-to-bill ratio above our 1.2x target, providing strong future visibility."

Additionally, for 2027, we are targeting a gross profit margin range of 8.5% to 9.0%, supported by continued margin expansion through reduced seasonality, improved pricing, increased productivity and operating efficiencies, and the quality of our growing portfolio of bid opportunities."
The Company estimates that approximately $2 billion of MSA contract value will be renewed by year-end and forecasts that the full year book-to-bill will exceed its 1.2x target.
The Company has updated full-year 2026 guidance.
The conference call will be webcast live on the Company’s investor relations (IR) website at https://investor.centuri.com.
Based on guidance from the SEC, we may use the IR section of our website to communicate with investors.

The statements in this press release are (i) made as of the date of this press release, even if subsequently made available by Centuri on its website or otherwise, and (ii) based on assumptions and assessments made by our management in light of their experience and perceptions of historical trends, current conditions, expected future developments and other factors they believe to be appropriate.
We are unable to provide reconciliations for forward-looking non-GAAP measures without unreasonable efforts due to our inability to project non-recurring expenses and events.

statements.t: We also serve complementary, attractive and growing end markets such as distributed power projects and data centers.
Accordingly, our operating results in any particular period may not be indicative of the results that can be expected for any other period.

While these costs moderated during the third fiscal quarter of 2026, we expect our labor-related costs will continue to be impacted by our investments in attracting and retaining skilled labor in this highly competitive environment for utility infrastructure services.
Generally, our contracts provide that the customer is responsible for supplying the materials for their projects.

Fluctuations in the price or availability of materials and equipment that we or our customers utilize could impact (positively or negatively, as applicable) costs to complete projects or result in the postponement of projects.

Although certain of our customers have experienced previous disruptions in their supply chain for certain project materials, most of our customers have generally been able to procure the necessary materials in a timely manner.
We believe we have taken steps to secure delivery of a sufficient amount of equipment and do not anticipate any significant disruptions with respect to our fleet in the near-term.
Alternatively, these severe weather events can also delay projects, negatively impacting our results of operations.
The availability of transportation and transmission capacity can also impact demand for our services, including energy generation, electric grid and pipeline construction projects.
The highly competitive nature of our industry can result in changes in the levels of activity, project mix and moreover the profitability of the services we provide.

We compete with a number of regional and national utility infrastructure services companies for contracts and labor, and competitors may be awarded work that we seek, which could reduce our revenue and utilization levels.

These changes may create opportunities that increase demand for our services or, alternatively, may delay, reduce or increase the cost of customer projects, and we cannot predict their timing or effect on our results of operations.
Additionally, customer investment in data center-related infrastructure intended to support the related increasing power demands represents a growing opportunity for us.

Our ability to capitalize on these opportunities will depend in part on the pace of permitting and regulatory approval of these projects by our customers, which may be affected by, among other factors, developments at the federal, state and local levels in legislative, regulatory and community initiatives with respect to data centers or a slowdown, reprioritization or technological shift in artificial…
Postponement or a reduction in the scope of customer projects could affect the timing of our revenue and our results of operations.
Our backlog includes data center-related projects only when we believe the applicable customer budgets have been approved and required permitting has been obtained.
Margins for our projects may vary from period to period due to changes in the volume or type of work performed and the pricing structure of our projects.

Additionally, factors such as site conditions, project location, competition for skilled craft labor, labor shortages, weather events, environmental restrictions, regulatory delays, protests, political activity, legal challenges, or the performance of third parties may adversely impact our project performance.

We attempt to recover anticipated increases in the cost of labor, equipment, fuel and materials not purchased by customers through price escalation provisions that allow us to adjust billing rates for certain major contracts annually; by considering the estimated effect of such increases when bidding or pricing new work; or by entering into back-to-back contracts with suppliers and subcontractors.

Backlog differs from remaining performance obligations disclosed in “Note 3 — Revenue and Related Balance Sheet Accounts” to the condensed consolidated financial statements, as remaining performance obligations are limited to contractually obligated revenue on our contracts that exceed one year, which is typically only bid projects, whereas backlog is inclusive of all contracts regardless of length and includes…
The construction industry is capital intensive, and we expect to continue to incur capital expenditures to meet anticipated needs for our services.

Under the Securitization Facility, certain of our designated subsidiaries have sold or contributed, and will continue to sell or contribute, their accounts receivable and contract assets generated in the ordinary course of their business and certain related assets to the indirect, wholly owned bankruptcy-remote Special Purpose Entity (“SPE”) we created specifically for this purpose.
